problem: The function $y=f(x)$ satisfies the differential equation ${y}^{′}={y}^{2}+{x}^{2}.$ Given that the point $(1,1)$ lies on the graph of the function, what is the value of ${{y}^{″}|}_{(1,1)}?$

feedback.problem:
The function $y=f(x)$ satisfies the differential equation 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=2y+4\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Given that the point $P(0,0)$ lies on the graph of the function, evaluate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}$ at $P.$

$\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\,{|}_{(0,0)}=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
To find an expression for the second derivative, we differentiate the equation with respect to $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2y+4\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2y)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y)-4\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =2\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-4\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the given expression for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ into the above and simplify the resulting expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =2(2y+4\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-4\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =4y+8\operatorname{cos}⁡x-4\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute the coordinates of our point into the above expression for the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\,{|}_{(0,0)} & =(4y+8\operatorname{cos}⁡x-4\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,{|}_{(0,0)} \\  & =4(0)+8\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(0) \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$
